summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was readmitted within 36 hours of discharge due to recurrent abdominal pain and nausea, consistent with a flare. She was managed with bowel rest, TPN via her stable PICC line, IV hydromorphone initially, and antiemetics. The pain service recommended increasing gabapentin to three times daily and starting amitriptyline at night for neuropathic pain. Her symptoms gradually improved, allowing transition to oral pain medications and advancement to a soft diet. An MRCP showed stable chronic pancreatitis without acute complications. She was discharged home on TPN with visiting nurse support, new prescriptions for gabapentin and amitriptyline, and a follow-up appointment with her gastroenterologist in one week.
